candidate.title: Psalm 104 and Its Parallels in Pharaoh Akhenaten's Hymn
candidate.ask_addressed: Quote the Egyptian primary texts that threads depend on: ... the Great Hymn to the Aten (Amarna, c. 1350 BCE)
candidate.quote: This seems self-evident to me, but has been debated endlessly over the past century.
candidate.summary: Koller argues themes of the Aten hymn recur in Psalm 104 and says the relation 'has been debated endlessly'; he names Dion (1991) and Day (2016) as presentations leaving 'no doubt'.
candidate.limits: Author's own stance is that the connection is clear; a popular-scholarly platform, not peer-reviewed. Route not documented.

strand.what: creation-by-the-sun hymn motifs (night animals, human labour by day, sea creatures)

reason: strand_unsupported: the quoted sentence ('This seems self-evident to me, but has been debated endlessly') is a footnote about whether the Psalmist is monotheistic, not about the Aten hymn-Psalm 104 relationship; the page does carry the parallel argument elsewhere but the quoted passage does not support the strand.

candidate.title: The Papyrus Ebers (Bryan 1930), magic with the remedy
candidate.ask_addressed: and any Egyptian text describing a chemical or technical process (for example the Ebers papyrus recipes)
candidate.quote: Finally they resorted to Magic, plus the Brain-of-a-Tortoise mixed with Honey
candidate.summary: The same chapter mixes spell-recitation with the recipes. A caution that Ebers is not a 'technical process' text in the sense of a chemistry or metallurgy manual.
candidate.limits: Bryan's 1930 gloss; modern work (not opened) separates the empirical and magical strands differently.
